name: Convex hull via Andrew's monotone chain

variants.task: Create /tmp/eval_hull/hull.py — reads from stdin: line 1 is T (test cases). Each case: line A is N (number of input points), then N lines of 'x y' integer coordinates. For each case, output line 1 = K (hull vertex count), then K lines of 'x y' for hull vertices in CCW order starting from the lexicographically smallest point. Do NOT include collinear points along hull edges. Inputs are guaranteed to have at least 3 distinct non-collinear points. Use Andrew's monotone chain. A sample input is provided at /tmp/eval_hull/input.txt; no expected-output file is provided. Validation runs your program on that sample plus additional hidden cases in the same format and compares the output, so implement the general algorithm rather than printing fixed answers.

validation.script: set -e; cd /tmp/eval_hull && python3 hull.py < input.txt > out.txt && diff -u expected.txt out.txt && echo OK

variants.task: Create /tmp/eval_hull/hull.zig — reads from stdin: line 1 is T (test cases). Each case: a line with N, then N lines of 'x y' integer coordinates. For each case output line 1 = K (hull vertex count), then K lines of 'x y' for the hull vertices in CCW order starting from the lexicographically smallest point, no collinear edge points. Inputs have at least 3 distinct non-collinear points. Use Andrew's monotone chain. Use Zig 0.16+ idioms. Entrypoint: `pub fn main(init: std.process.Init) !void`. For stdio, the rich API (`takeDelimiter`, `appendRemainingUnlimited`, `print`, `writeAll`, `flush`) lives on the `std.Io.Reader`/`Writer` *interface*, NOT on the concrete `std.Io.File.Reader`/`Writer`. Reach the interface via `&fr.interface`. Canonical setup: `var in_buf: [4096]u8 = undefined; var fr = std.Io.File.stdin().reader(init.io, &in_buf); const r = &fr.interface;` and the symmetric writer. Then `try r.takeDelimiter('\n')` (returns `?[]u8`, null at EOF) for line-by-line, or `try r.appendRemainingUnlimited(init.arena.allocator(), &list)` to slurp. Always `try w.flush()` before return — output is buffered. Strict-default footguns (errors, not warnings, in 0.16): rename unused params to `_`, discard unused locals with `_ = x;`, prefer `const` over `var` when not mutated. Use `std.Io` (capital I), not `std.io`. Will be compiled with `zig build-exe -O ReleaseFast hull.zig` and tested by piping `input.txt` through stdin and checking against `expected.txt` (or via a check.py validator). A sample input is provided at /tmp/eval_hull/input.txt; no expected-output file is provided. Validation runs your program on that sample plus additional hidden cases in the same format and compares the output, so implement the general algorithm rather than printing fixed answers.

validation.script: set -e; cd /tmp/eval_hull && zig build-exe -O ReleaseFast hull.zig && ./hull < input.txt > out.txt && diff -u expected.txt out.txt && echo OK
